mimo/06-product-planning/RESPONSE.md

RESPONSE — three riskiest assumptions

  1. Offline auth stays usable for a full shift (A1/D5). If tokens die or the server demands fresh auth while the inspector is in a basement, every other offline feature is unreachable. This is the single point of failure before capture even starts. Mitigation: device-bound cached credentials gated by a daily biometric/passcode unlock (D5); validate on real devices in S0 before building anything else.

  2. Conflict policy of "server (supervisor) wins on same-field edit" is acceptable to inspectors and compliance (A8/D4). If field staff cannot accept losing a locally edited value (even with an audit copy and a toast), the product needs merge UI or offline edit leases — a large scope increase the brief explicitly forbids. Mitigation: put the conflict dialog in front of pilot users in S0 and treat any "I lost my notes" complaint as a gate failure, not a support ticket.

  3. The 24h post-acceptance local purge requirement can be met with a purge receipt (hash list) rather than a local audit replica (A4/D6). If regulators require on-device audit history after acceptance, purge and retention collide, the data model changes, and mobile storage may never be demonstrably clean. Mitigation: confirm with compliance before M4; the receipt design is a cheap extension point but the underlying deletion is not reversible, so this must be locked before the first real acceptance in the pilot.

mimo/06-product-planning/BRIEF.md

Offline inspection brief

Inspectors use company-managed tablets in basements with no signal. Today, a lost connection after opening an inspection can discard notes. They need to open assigned inspections, fill forms, take up to 40 photos, and collect a signature offline. Connectivity may return intermittently. Supervisors can edit the same inspection from the web. Regulations require an audit history and removal of local customer data within 24 hours after an inspection is accepted. Existing server APIs use REST with integer record versions. The mobile app has SQLite but currently treats it as a read-through cache. Product wants a pilot before broad rollout and does not want a full collaborative editor.

mimo/06-product-planning/PLAN.md

Plan: Offline work for tablet building-inspection app

1. Assumptions (explicit)

# Assumption If wrong
A1 Company-managed tablets have a local auth session (token or cert) that remains valid for a full offline shift (≥ 24h) Need offline-issued short-lived credentials or a device unlock flow
A2 Assigned inspections can be listed and fully downloaded before signal is lost; inspectors know which assignment they will work Need an always-cached "my queue" and forced prefetch on assignment
A3 Acceptance (supervisor sign-off) is a server-side state transition; the tablet only submits, it does not accept Acceptance path also needs offline rules; scope grows
A4 "Removal of local customer data within 24h after acceptance" means: after sync confirms accepted, the device may purge that inspection; no need to keep a local audit replica Must retain a minimal audit stub locally and prove retention to auditors
A5 Forms are structured (schema-versioned fields + free-text notes), not freeform documents Richer offline editing model required
A6 Photo metadata (time, inspector, inspection id) is the compliance artifact; exact original bytes may be recompressed for transfer Must keep original bytes bit-for-bit
A7 Integer record versions on the server are monotonically increasing per inspection record and can be used as sync tokens Need a richer revision/history API
A8 One inspector owns field edits on a given inspection during a session; supervisor edits are rare and can lose to "last writer with version check" rather than merge True multi-author field-level merge is required (out of scope per product)
A9 Pilot devices can receive app updates and server feature flags; pilot users tolerate occasional re-sync prompts No remote control channel; bake everything into releases

2. Goals / non-goals

Goals

  • Open assigned inspections, fill forms, attach up to 40 photos, capture a signature with zero connectivity.
  • Survive intermittent connectivity with automatic retry; never silently discard user-entered data.
  • Keep a tamper-evident audit history of field-level changes and sync events.
  • Purge customer data from the device within 24h of server-side acceptance.
  • Pilot with a small cohort before broad rollout.

Non-goals

  • Real-time collaborative editing / CRDTs / presence.
  • Offline creation of brand-new inspections.
  • Offline editing by supervisors on the web (web stays online-only).
  • Cross-device handoff of an in-progress offline inspection.

3. User flow

  1. Prep (online): Inspector signs in, opens My assignments. App downloads each assigned inspection (schema + current answers + photo list + version) and marks it local-ready. Badge: "Available offline".
  2. Site (offline): Inspector opens a local-ready inspection. Forms save to SQLite on every field commit. Photos write to app-private storage with a local blob id; thumbnails cached. Signature captured as vector + raster; hash recorded.
  3. Intermittent sync: When the network returns (app foreground, or background fetch every N minutes when permitted), the app drains a per-inspection outbox: metadata/answers first, then attachments in priority order (signature > small fields > photos). Progress UI shows pending count. Retry with exponential backoff + jitter; never drop an outbox entry without either success or explicit user confirmation of abandon.
  4. Submit offline: Inspector marks the inspection ready-to-submit. If offline, it queues as the final outbox item. On successful submit, server returns new version + submitted state.
  5. Acceptance (supervisor, web): Supervisor reviews, may edit (online). Server bumps version and records audit. When state becomes accepted, the next device sync response includes accepted + purge-after timestamp (accepted_at + 24h).
  6. Purge: App deletes local answers, photos, signature, and derived thumbnails for that inspection at purge time (or on next launch if device was off), keeps only a purge receipt (inspection id, purge time, content hashes) unless A4 says otherwise, and reports purge to the server for compliance.

4. Scope boundaries

  • Offline is available only for inspections that were successfully opened/downloaded while online at least once ("local-ready set").
  • Edits are whole-inspection last-writer-wins at field granularity with version precondition; no merge UI in v1 (conflict surface is a dialog, see §7).
  • Photos: up to 40 per inspection, compressed for upload (configurable max edge / JPEG quality), originals retained locally until purge.
  • Signature: one inspector signature offline; countersign (if any) is online-only in v1.
  • No offline export/email of reports; report PDF generation stays server-side.

5. Local data model (SQLite + blob store)

Tables (illustrative):

  • inspections(id PK, server_version, state, assigned_to, schema_id, schema_version, downloaded_at, accepted_at, purge_after, dirty)
  • answers(inspection_id, field_id, value_text, value_num, value_bool, updated_at, updated_by, local_rev, sync_state) — PK (inspection_id, field_id)
  • attachments(id PK, inspection_id, kind /*photo|signature*/, local_path, sha256, bytes, mime, captured_at, server_id NULL, upload_state, retries)
  • outbox(id PK, inspection_id, op /*upsert_answers|upload_attachment|submit|ack_purge*/, payload_json, created_at, next_attempt_at, attempts, state)
  • audit_events(id PK, inspection_id, at, actor, device_id, event_type /*edit|photo_add|sign|sync_ok|sync_fail|submit|purge*/, field_id NULL, old_hash, new_hash, prev_event_hash, event_hash) — hash chain per inspection
  • schema_cache(schema_id, version, form_json, fetched_at)

Blobs in files/attachments/<sha256> (content-addressed). DB stores only hashes + paths. All writes go through a single repository layer so purge and audit cannot be bypassed.

local_rev is a per-device monotonic counter for idempotent outbox identity; the server still owns server_version.

6. Sync protocol

Keep REST; extend, don't replace.

  1. Pull GET /inspections/{id}?since_version=v → record + version + state. Also GET /assignments for queue refresh (online only).
  2. Push POST /inspections/{id}/changes with:
    • base_version (precondition),
    • client_change_id (UUID, idempotency key),
    • field upserts (only dirty fields) + client_rev,
    • optional op=submit. Response: 200 new server_version, or 409 with server field snapshot for conflict handling, or 422 schema/validation error (do not retry blindly — surface to user).
  3. Attachments POST /inspections/{id}/attachments (multipart or resumable upload session for photos; chunk size ~1–2 MB). Server returns server_id. Upload is content-hash idempotent. Signature uploads first and is required before submit succeeds.
  4. Purge ack POST /inspections/{id}/purge-ack with device id, purge time, list of deleted hashes.
  5. Ordering per inspection: answer upserts → attachment uploads → submit → (later) purge-ack. Across inspections, outbox is parallelizable but bounded (2 workers) to protect radio/battery.
  6. Idempotency: every push carries client_change_id; server stores it and returns the original result on replay (covers timeout-after-commit).
  7. Clock skew: server timestamps are authoritative for accepted_at / purge_after; device uses them verbatim.

7. Conflict policy

Product decision: no collaborative editor. Policy:

  • Every push requires base_version == server_version, else 409.
  • On 409, app compares dirty local fields vs server snapshot:
    • If disjoint field sets → auto-rebase: retry push with new base_version (still recorded in audit).
    • If same field edited → local field loses (server wins) for supervisor-originated changes; show a non-blocking toast listing overwritten fields, and keep the local discarded value in audit_events (not as an editable answer).
    • If local has submit pending and server moved past submitted/accepted → drop local submit, adopt server state.
  • Photo/signature blobs never conflict (append-only by hash); duplicates deduped server-side.
  • Rationale: supervisors are the reviewers; their online corrections are authoritative. Field-level LWW avoids silent data loss better than whole-record LWW.

8. Attachments

  • Cap 40 photos/inspection (enforced locally and server-side). Show remaining count.
  • Local pipeline: capture → downscale preview → store original → enqueue upload of transfer encoding (config: max edge 2048, JPEG q≈80) plus EXIF time. Strip precise GPS by default (policy flag).
  • Resumable uploads; cancel/retry UI; upload only on Wi-Fi toggle (default on for company-managed devices).
  • Signature stored as PNG/SVG + device-local cert binding (see §9). Hash of signature payload written to audit chain before first upload attempt.

9. Security

  • Auth tokens in platform keystore/Keychain; biometric/passcode device unlock required before first offline edit of the day (gate for offline use of cached credentials).
  • App-private storage; no customer data on shared storage. Screen capture discouraged via OS flags where available (not compliance-critical).
  • All sync traffic TLS 1.2+; certificate pinning optional for pilot (decide via D1).
  • Field-level values never logged; logs carry ids/hashes only.
  • Remote wipe / selective purge command path (MDM or server "revoke inspection" push) — MDM wipe covers lost devices; in-app purge covers retention.
  • Signature integrity: hash of signature image + inspection id + schema version chained into audit; server verifies hash on submit.

10. Migration / backfill

  • Server: add client_change_id idempotency store, attachment upload sessions, purge-ack endpoint, accepted_at on inspections. Additive, versioned (Accept: application/vnd.insp.v2+json).
  • Device: migrate answers table from cache semantics to durable outbox-backed store (local_rev, sync_state columns; backfill local_rev=0). Migration is transactional; on failure app falls back to read-only cache mode and forces resync rather than risking corruption.
  • Existing cached inspections are re-downloaded once (treat as not local-ready until re-fetched) — simplest correct backfill.
  • Audit chain starts at migration time; a server-side audit_created root event anchors the chain per inspection.

11. Observability

  • Client metrics (aggregated, no PII): outbox depth/age, sync success/409/422 rates, attachment upload retries/time-to-drain, purge latency after accepted_at, crash-free sessions on pilot builds.
  • Server metrics: 409 rate by field, idempotent replays, purge-ack lag, attachment integrity mismatches.
  • Per-inspection audit chain export endpoint for regulators (server-side; device contributes events via sync).
  • Alerting: purge-ack lag > 20h in pilot → page on-call (compliance clock).

12. Staged rollout

Stage Cohort Gate to next
S0 Internal dogfood (2–3 devices, synthetic buildings) 2 full offline-to-accept-to-purge cycles per device; zero silent data loss
S1 Pilot: 5–15 inspectors, one region, real jobs ≥ 95% sessions complete offline path without support ticket; purge-ack lag p95 < 12h; 409 auto-rebase success ≥ 90% of conflicts
S2 Expand regions + supervisor conflict tooling polish S1 metrics hold for 2 weeks of real volume
S3 Broad rollout No open Sev-1/2 from S2

Feature flag offline_mode (server-driven) plus minimum app version flag. Kill switch flips devices to read-only cache behavior on next connect.

13. Rollback

  • Flag off: devices stop accepting offline edits; pending outboxes still drain (never discard). New edits require connectivity.
  • App release rollback: schema migrations written backward-compatible within one minor (additive columns only for 2 releases) so store rollback doesn't brick local DB.
  • Server rollback: v2 routes are additive; v1 clients unaffected. Idempotency store retained.
  • Data rollback: purge is destructive by design — not reversible; rollback of the feature does not resurrect purged device data (server remains system of record).
  • Declare explicitly: accept loss of in-flight offline edits only via user-mediated "abandon changes" — no automatic rollback path drops outbox.

14. Testing

  • Unit: outbox state machine, conflict rebase/field-diff, audit hash chain, purge scheduler.
  • Integration: REST sync against staging with fault injection (timeouts after commit, 409 storms, chunked upload interrupt).
  • Device lab: airplane-mode runs for full inspection + 40 photos + signature; intermittent network (monkey/chaos profile); force-quit mid-upload; clock skew.
  • Compliance tests: simulated accepted → verify purge within 24h including device-off window at purge time; audit chain verification job.
  • Pilot exit checklist = S1 gate metrics above.

15. Milestone sequence (no dates, no staffing)

M1 — Offline capture core (depends: schema cache, device storage migration)

  • Durable answers + local attachments + outbox; no network required after download.
  • AC: airplane-mode inspection completion with 40 photos + signature intact after force-quit.

M2 — Sync engine (depends: M1, server idempotent change API, attachment upload API)

  • Ordered drain, retries, 409 auto-rebase, field-conflict surfacing.
  • AC: fault-injection suite green; replaying client_change_id yields single commit.

M3 — Submit + supervisor convergence (depends: M2)

  • Offline submit queue; server 409 policy as in §7; audit chain upload.
  • AC: concurrent supervisor edit vs offline submit converges deterministically; audit chain verifies.

M4 — Retention & purge (depends: M3, accepted_at + purge-ack API)

  • Purge scheduling, receipts, compliance metric.
  • AC: purge-ack p95 < 12h in S0/S1; regulator export job runs clean.

M5 — Pilot hardened (depends: M1–M4, feature flag, observability)

  • Kill switch, Wi-Fi-only toggle, support tooling (per-device sync dump), S0 exit.
  • AC: S0 checklist passed; docs for field support.

M6 — Pilot & evaluate (depends: M5)

  • S1 cohort run; go/no-go for S2.
  • AC: S1 gate metrics met or explicit product sign-off to iterate.

Dependencies: M1→M2→M3→M4 is the critical path; M5 can overlap late M4 (flags/observability); M6 is strictly gated.

16. Decisions required before implementation (with recommendations)

ID Decision Recommendation Why
D1 TLS pinning on/off Off for pilot, measure; decide before S2 Pinning complicates enterprise proxy debugging; pilot risk is low on managed networks
D2 Photo transfer encoding vs originals Upload compressed derivative + hashes of original; keep original until purge Bandwidth in basements/street 4G; regulators accept hash-anchored originals
D3 GPS in EXIF Strip by default; site id is the location record Avoid precise home location retention; simpler purge surface
D4 Conflict: who wins on same-field edit Server (supervisor) wins; local discarded value kept in audit only Matches "not a collaborative editor"; reviewers are authoritative
D5 Offline auth lifetime Require daily unlock (biometric/passcode) to use cached creds; session ≤ 7 days device-bound Limits lost-device exposure while keeping full-shift offline
D6 Purge receipt contents Store id, times, hash list only — no field values Satisfies A4 with minimal residual risk; easy to extend if auditors demand more
D7 Attachment upload radio policy Wi-Fi preferred, cellular allowed after 30 min backlog Pilot devices are cellular-enabled; don't strand evidence
D8 Schema evolution while offline Pin schema_version at download; edits with old schema still accepted if field ids stable; force re-download if schema breaking: true Avoids mid-form surprise; server remains flexible
D9 Signature acceptance offline Capture full signature packet offline; mark submitted only after signature hash reaches server Signature is the legal artifact; don't let submit succeed without it
D10 Kill-switch behavior Read-only cache mode, outbox drains, no new offline edits Never destroy user work when disabling the feature

17. Open questions (explicitly deferred)

  • Countersignature workflow and whether it needs offline support (assume no for pilot).
  • Cross-inspection batching for sites with many units.
  • Long-term device audit retention if A4 is later rejected by compliance.

mimo/06-product-planning/TASK.md

Task 06 — Product and engineering planning: offline inspection sync

Create PLAN.md for adding offline work to a tablet-based building inspection app. Use BRIEF.md as the only product input.

The plan should make assumptions explicit and cover user flow, scope boundaries, local data model, sync protocol, conflict policy, attachments, security, migration/backfill, observability, staged rollout, rollback, and testing. Include a milestone sequence with dependencies and acceptance criteria. Identify the decisions that must be made before implementation and offer a recommendation for each. Avoid fake dates and unjustified staffing estimates.

Write RESPONSE.md summarizing the three riskiest assumptions. Work only in this directory.

Evaluation 4.25 / 10 graded blind as submission H

The weakest plan. It conflates 'synced' with 'accepted' and starts the purge at synced_at+24h, then asks in open questions which one applies. It puts offline creation in scope despite assigned-only work. After 3 retries it marks an inspection as a conflict. It treats a base_version 409 as idempotency, adds a version column the brief says already exists, and assumes Android/Room/Play Integrity. It includes staffing and duration estimates (3 QA engineers, 1/2/4-week stages, a 2-day spike, '2-3x engineering effort'). Rollback via binary downgrade can drop tables.

Strengths

  • Has a concrete SQL schema and an endpoint list; PII excluded from logs

Weaknesses

  • purge_after = synced_at + 24h, and the user flow says 'Server accepts -> inspection marked synced; local customer data purged within 24h'
  • Unjustified staffing and durations: '3 QA engineers + 2 inspectors (1 week)', '50 inspectors across 3 regions (4 weeks)', 'Backend spike (2 days)'
  • Server-wins LWW plus 'Max 3 retries per inspection before marking conflict'; idempotency only via a version check
  • No explicit assumptions section; M1 depends on 'BRIEF.md approved' with no decision or validation gate
Evidence the grader checked

  • H/PLAN.md:275-277 stage table; H/RESPONSE.md:37,44
  • H/PLAN.md:160-165 retries/idempotency; :240-242 adds version column

Objective checks

Files

nemotron-3-ultra/06-product-planning/RESPONSE.md

Riskiest Assumptions — RESPONSE.md

1. "Tablets reliably regain connectivity within 24 hours for purge compliance"

Why it's risky: The 24-hour local-data-purge requirement (regulation-driven) depends on the tablet syncing to the server so synced_at is set. If an inspector works in a basement for 3 days without signal, local PII persists beyond the regulatory window. The brief states "connectivity may return intermittently" but doesn't bound the maximum offline duration.

Impact if wrong: Regulatory violation; potential fines; data breach liability if tablet is lost/stolen during extended offline period.

Mitigation in plan:

  • Purge timer starts at server-acknowledged synced_at, not local completion
  • Daily background job enforces purge; logs missed deadlines
  • MDM can remote-wipe on demand

Validation needed in pilot: Measure actual offline durations across pilot team; add telemetry for "hours since last sync." If >5% of inspections exceed 24h offline, we need a fallback (e.g., local purge after 24h with server reconciliation on next sync, accepting brief inconsistency).

2. "Last-Writer-Wins per field is acceptable for all regulated inspection fields"

Why it's risky: The brief mentions "regulations require an audit history" but not whether specific fields (e.g., "pass/fail", "hazard_present") require human review on conflict. LWW silently discards the inspector's offline value when a supervisor edits the same field. If a safety-critical field is overwritten without traceability, the audit log shows that a conflict occurred but not why the supervisor's value was chosen.

Impact if wrong: Failed audit; legal challenge if a failed inspection appears as "passed" due to silent LWW; erosion of inspector trust.

Mitigation in plan:

  • All conflicts recorded in audit log with both values
  • Conflict banner forces inspector acknowledgment
  • Config flag per field type to escalate to mandatory manual resolution

Validation needed in pilot: Review every conflict with compliance officer during pilot. Classify fields as "LWW-safe" vs. "requires manual." If any regulated field falls in the latter, the config flag becomes a launch blocker.

3. "Existing REST + integer version APIs can support bidirectional sync without server-side architectural changes"

Why it's risky: The brief states "Existing server APIs use REST with integer record versions." The sync protocol designed here assumes the server can: (a) accept a base_version for optimistic concurrency, (b) return merged results with conflict arrays, (c) serve audit logs since a version, and (d) assign server IDs to offline-created records. If the current API layer lacks version-checking middleware, audit tables, or idempotency keys, the server work expands from "add endpoints" to "rewrite data access layer."

Impact if wrong: 2-3x engineering effort on server side; pilot delay; potential schema migrations on production DB affecting web supervisors.

Mitigation in plan:

  • Server migration adds version column + audit_log table behind feature flag
  • Sync endpoint spec defined upfront for backend team estimation
  • Pilot uses isolated test environment

Validation needed in pilot: Backend spike (2 days) to implement POST /sync against a copy of production schema before M3. If version checks require row-level locks that deadlock under load, we may need a separate sync service — a major scope change.

nemotron-3-ultra/06-product-planning/BRIEF.md

Offline inspection brief

Inspectors use company-managed tablets in basements with no signal. Today, a lost connection after opening an inspection can discard notes. They need to open assigned inspections, fill forms, take up to 40 photos, and collect a signature offline. Connectivity may return intermittently. Supervisors can edit the same inspection from the web. Regulations require an audit history and removal of local customer data within 24 hours after an inspection is accepted. Existing server APIs use REST with integer record versions. The mobile app has SQLite but currently treats it as a read-through cache. Product wants a pilot before broad rollout and does not want a full collaborative editor.

nemotron-3-ultra/06-product-planning/PLAN.md

Offline Inspection Sync — PLAN.md

1. User Flow

Inspector (tablet, offline-first)

  1. App launches → loads assigned inspections from local SQLite (pre-synced when online)
  2. Opens inspection → all form sections, existing notes, and thumbnails available locally
  3. Fills form fields, adds notes, captures up to 40 photos (stored as local files + DB records)
  4. Collects customer signature via on-screen canvas → stored as PNG locally
  5. Taps "Complete" → inspection moves to pending_sync state; local UI shows sync status badge
  6. When connectivity returns → background sync uploads changes, downloads supervisor edits
  7. Server accepts → inspection marked synced; local customer data purged within 24h

Supervisor (web, online)

  1. Views inspections in dashboard (real-time from server)
  2. Edits form fields or adds annotations → creates new server version
  3. Changes propagate to inspector's tablet on next sync

Conflict scenario: Inspector edited field X offline; supervisor edited same field X online. Sync detects version mismatch → applies conflict policy (see §5).

2. Scope Boundaries

In Scope Out of Scope
Offline create/edit of assigned inspections Real-time collaborative editing (Google Docs style)
Photo capture (≤40/inspection) + signature capture Offline supervisor editing
Background sync with retry/backoff Cross-inspection dependencies
Audit log (server-authoritative) Offline mode for unassigned inspections
24h local data purge after server accept Multi-device inspector sessions
Pilot with 1 team (~10 inspectors) Full migration of historical inspections to new schema

Assumptions:

  • Tablets are company-managed (MDM enrolled), Android 10+, 64GB+ storage
  • Inspectors work solo per inspection; no handoff mid-inspection
  • Server remains REST + integer versions; no GraphQL/WebSocket investment
  • Pilot validates architecture before broad rollout

3. Local Data Model (SQLite)

-- Core tables
CREATE TABLE inspections (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,              -- server ID
  local_id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,       -- UUID for offline-created
  server_version INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- last known server version
  status TEXT NOT NULL,                -- 'draft' | 'pending_sync' | 'synced' | 'conflict'
  assigned_inspector_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  form_data_json TEXT NOT NULL,        -- JSON blob of all form fields
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,         -- unix ms
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  synced_at INTEGER,                   -- null until server accepts
  purge_after INTEGER                  -- synced_at + 24h (ms)
);

CREATE TABLE photos (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  inspection_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES inspections(id),
  local_path TEXT NOT NULL,            -- file:// path in app sandbox
  server_id INTEGER,                   -- null until uploaded
  caption TEXT,
  sort_order INTEGER NOT NULL,
  uploaded_at INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE signatures (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  inspection_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES inspections(id),
  local_path TEXT NOT NULL,
  server_id INTEGER,
  signer_name TEXT,
  signed_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  uploaded_at INTEGER
);

-- Sync metadata
CREATE TABLE sync_state (
  key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT NOT NULL
); -- e.g., 'last_full_sync_ms', 'pending_count'

-- Audit trail (append-only, mirrors server)
CREATE TABLE audit_log (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  inspection_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  actor_type TEXT NOT NULL,            -- 'inspector' | 'supervisor' | 'system'
  actor_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  action TEXT NOT NULL,                -- 'created' | 'field_changed' | 'photo_added' | 'signed' | 'synced' | 'purged'
  field_name TEXT,                     -- null for non-field actions
  old_value TEXT,
  new_value TEXT,
  timestamp INTEGER NOT NULL,
  server_version INTEGER NOT NULL
);

Key invariants

  • inspections.local_id generated on first offline create; server_id assigned on first successful sync
  • server_version monotonic; used for optimistic concurrency
  • purge_after set only after synced_at confirmed; enforced by daily background job
  • Photos/signatures stored as files; DB holds metadata only (avoids SQLite bloat)

4. Sync Protocol

Transport: HTTPS POST to existing REST endpoints; multipart/form-data for attachments.

Endpoints (extend existing)

Endpoint Purpose
POST /api/v1/inspections/sync Bidirectional sync: upload pending, download changes
POST /api/v1/inspections/{id}/photos Upload photo (returns server_id)
POST /api/v1/inspections/{id}/signature Upload signature
GET /api/v1/inspections/{id}/audit Fetch audit history (for compliance view)

Request/Response (sync endpoint)

// Request
{
  "device_id": "tablet-uuid",
  "inspector_id": 123,
  "since_version": 456,                 // client's last known server version
  "inspections": [                      // only inspections with local changes
    {
      "local_id": "uuid",
      "server_id": 789,                 // null if never synced
      "base_version": 450,              // version client last saw
      "form_data": { ... },
      "photos": [ { "local_id": 1, "caption": "..." } ],
      "signature": { "local_id": 1, "signer_name": "John" }
    }
  ]
}

// Response
{
  "server_version": 472,
  "inspections": [
    {
      "server_id": 789,
      "local_id": "uuid",
      "version": 472,
      "form_data": { ... },             // merged result
      "conflicts": [                    // empty if auto-merged
        { "field": "roof_condition", "server_value": "OK", "local_value": "Damaged" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "deleted_inspection_ids": [999],      // supervisor deleted
  "audit_entries": [ ... ]              // new audit rows since since_version
}

Retry/Backoff

  • Exponential backoff: 5s, 15s, 45s, 2m, 5m, 15m (max)
  • Max 3 retries per inspection before marking conflict requiring manual review
  • Sync runs: on app foreground, every 15min when online, on connectivity change broadcast

Idempotency

  • Client includes base_version; server rejects if version mismatch (409)
  • Photo/signature uploads use content-hash dedupe; safe to retry

5. Conflict Policy

Default: Last-Writer-Wins (LWW) per field with audit trail

  • Server compares base_version → if match, accepts; if mismatch, computes field-level diff
  • For each conflicting field: server value wins; local value stored in conflicts array in response
  • Inspector sees conflict banner on next app open; can view diff and manually override
  • Supervisor edits always win on server (authoritative); inspector cannot force-push

Exceptions (require manual resolution)

  • Signature mismatch (two signatures captured) → flag for compliance review
  • Photo count exceeds 40 after merge → reject sync, require inspector to delete

Decision required: Is LWW acceptable for all fields, or do regulated fields (e.g., "pass/fail") need mandatory manual resolution? → Recommend LWW for all but signature; add config flag per field type.

6. Attachments

Photos

  • Max 40 per inspection; max 8MB each (tablet camera default ~3-5MB)
  • Stored in app-private directory: files/inspections/{inspection_local_id}/photos/{uuid}.jpg
  • EXIF stripped on capture (privacy); GPS retained if permission granted
  • Upload: multipart, sequential, parallelism=2; progress shown per photo
  • Thumbnail (300px) generated locally for offline gallery; not uploaded

Signatures

  • Single PNG per inspection; vector path stored as JSON for potential re-render
  • Max 500KB; stored alongside photos
  • Uploaded with inspection sync payload (not separate endpoint)

Storage budget: ~40 photos × 8MB + signature ≈ 320MB worst case; well within 64GB.

Cleanup: Files deleted when inspection purged (24h post-sync); orphan sweep weekly.

7. Security

Data at rest (tablet)

  • Full-disk encryption (Android FBE) + app-level SQLCipher for SQLite
  • Photos/signatures encrypted via EncryptedFile (Jetpack Security)
  • Keys derived from hardware-backed keystore + inspector PIN (biometric unlock)

Data in transit

  • TLS 1.3 only; certificate pinning to company CA
  • Mutual TLS for device auth (client cert provisioned via MDM)

Authentication

  • Inspector: PIN + biometric; session token (JWT, 8h expiry) refreshed on sync
  • Supervisor: SSO (SAML/OIDC) on web; no offline access

Audit compliance

  • Server audit log immutable (append-only DB, WORM storage)
  • Tablet audit log mirrors server; tamper-evident via hash chain (each row includes hash of previous)
  • 24h purge: secure delete (overwrite + fsync) for customer PII fields (name, address, signature image)

Device trust

  • Attestation via Play Integrity API on each sync; reject rooted/compromised devices
  • Remote wipe via MDM if tablet lost

8. Migration / Backfill

Schema migration (tablet)

  • Use Room migrations (SQLite) for additive changes
  • New columns: local_id, server_version, status, purge_after, audit_log table
  • Backfill server_version from last successful API call timestamp
  • One-time migration script runs on first app launch after update

Server migration

  • Add version column to inspections table (integer, default 1)
  • Add audit_log table
  • Backfill version=1 for all existing inspections
  • Deploy behind feature flag; enable after tablet fleet updated

Historical data

  • Do NOT migrate pre-existing completed inspections to new offline schema
  • Read-only access via existing API; pilot only covers inspections created after launch

9. Observability

Client-side (tablet)

  • Structured logs (JSON) to local file; uploaded on sync
  • Metrics: sync_duration_ms, sync_result (success/conflict/error), pending_count, photo_upload_latency_p95, storage_used_mb
  • Crash/error reporting via existing Sentry/Play Console
  • Health check endpoint for MDM: GET /health → { last_sync_ms, pending, conflicts }

Server-side

  • Sync endpoint latency, error rates by code
  • Conflict rate by field, by inspector
  • Audit log write latency
  • Purge job success/failure count
  • Dashboard: "Inspections pending sync > 24h" alert

Correlation

  • device_id + inspection_id + sync_session_id (UUID per sync cycle) across client/server logs

10. Staged Rollout

Stage Audience Criteria to Advance
1. Internal dogfood 3 QA engineers + 2 inspectors (1 week) Zero data loss; sync success > 99%; conflict UX validated
2. Pilot team 10 inspectors, 2 supervisors (2 weeks) < 2% conflict rate; purge job 100% reliable; supervisor workflow accepted
3. Regional expansion 50 inspectors across 3 regions (4 weeks) Sync success > 99.5% at scale; MDM rollout smooth; support load manageable
4. General availability All inspectors Pilot metrics sustained; rollback tested; documentation complete

Gating: Each stage requires sign-off from Engineering Lead, Product, and Compliance.

11. Rollback Plan

Tablet app

  • Previous version remains in Play Console (track: internal → pilot → production)
  • Rollback = promote previous build to current track; users auto-update
  • Local DB forward-compatible: new columns nullable; old app ignores them
  • If schema migration ran: provide downgrade migration (drop new tables/columns) in rollback build

Server

  • Feature flag offline_sync_enabled (default false)
  • Rollback = flip flag false; existing sync endpoints return 503
  • Audit log and version columns retained (no data loss)
  • Database migration reversible (drop column) if needed

Data consistency on rollback

  • Inspections in pending_sync on tablet: user sees "sync unavailable" banner; data preserved locally
  • No server-side partial writes (sync is transactional per inspection)

12. Testing Strategy

Unit (CI, every PR)

  • Sync merge logic (LWW, conflict detection) — 100+ cases
  • Purge job (time boundaries, error handling)
  • Audit log hash chain verification
  • Photo dedupe by hash

Integration (nightly)

  • Full sync cycle against test server (Docker Compose)
  • Offline → online → offline transitions
  • Concurrent supervisor edit + inspector edit
  • Large payload (40 photos + signature) upload/download
  • Network flake simulation (Chaos Mesh)

Device lab (weekly)

  • 5 tablet models (various Android versions, storage tiers)
  • Cold start with 500 inspections cached
  • Battery drain during background sync
  • MDM policy enforcement (pinning, wipe)

Pilot UAT (manual)

  • Inspector completes 5 inspections offline in basement
  • Supervisor edits same inspection mid-flight
  • 24h purge verification (audit + file deletion)
  • Conflict resolution UI walkthrough

Compliance validation

  • Pen test on encrypted storage
  • Audit log immutability proof
  • 24h purge certification (third-party)

13. Milestone Sequence

Milestone Dependencies Acceptance Criteria
M1: Local data model + schema migration BRIEF.md approved Room migration passes; inspections CRUD works offline; unit tests > 90%
M2: Photo/signature capture + storage M1 40 photos + signature captured, stored encrypted, thumbnails render
M3: Sync protocol (upload only) M2 Pending inspections upload to test server; server returns version; idempotent retry works
M4: Sync protocol (download + merge) M3 Supervisor edits download; LWW merge produces correct result; conflicts surfaced
M5: Conflict UI + manual resolution M4 Inspector sees conflict banner; can view diff; override persists
M6: Audit log + 24h purge M3 Audit entries written on every change; purge job deletes PII + files at 24h+1m
M7: Security hardening M1-M6 SQLCipher + EncryptedFile; TLS pinning; Play Integrity attestation; pen test pass
M8: Observability + dashboards M3, M6 Metrics flowing; alerts firing on thresholds; correlation IDs work
M9: Pilot build + internal dogfood M7 Build distributed via Play Internal; dogfood team completes 10 inspections offline
M10: Pilot launch M9 sign-off 10 inspectors active; < 2% conflict rate; zero data loss in 2 weeks
M11: Regional expansion M10 sign-off 50 inspectors; sync success > 99.5%; support tickets < 5/week
M12: GA release M11 sign-off Rollback tested; docs complete; compliance sign-off

14. Decisions Required Before Implementation

Decision Recommendation Rationale
Conflict resolution: LWW vs. mandatory manual for regulated fields LWW for all fields except signature; add per-field-type config for future regulatory changes Simpler UX; audit trail captures both values; signature is legally sensitive
Photo upload: inline in sync payload vs. separate endpoints Separate endpoints (multipart) Allows parallel upload, resume, progress UI; keeps sync payload small
Local ID strategy: UUID vs. negative integers UUID (v4) Globally unique without coordination; works across devices if handoff ever added
Purge trigger: server-acknowledged synced_at vs. local timer Server-acknowledged synced_at Guarantees server has data before local delete; survives clock skew
Audit log storage: mirror on tablet vs. server-only Mirror on tablet (hash-chained) Offline compliance view; tamper evidence; server remains source of truth
Sync frequency: fixed interval vs. connectivity-driven + foreground Hybrid: foreground + connectivity change + 15min interval Balances battery, freshness, and "basement" reality
Device trust: Play Integrity only vs. + hardware attestation Play Integrity (BASIC) for pilot; evaluate STRONG for GA BASIC covers root/unlocked; STRONG requires newer hardware
Backfill historical inspections to new schema No — read-only via legacy API Avoids risky mass migration; pilot validates new flow on new inspections only
Supervisor offline editing Out of scope (per brief) Low ROI; supervisors have reliable connectivity
Maximum photo size / compression 8MB max, no client-side compression (preserve quality for compliance) Regulatory may require original resolution; storage budget allows it

15. Open Questions for Product

  1. Should inspectors be able to start a new inspection offline (not pre-assigned)?
  2. What happens if supervisor deletes an inspection that inspector has pending locally?
  3. Is 24h purge from synced_at or from "inspection accepted by supervisor"?
  4. Do we need to support inspector switching tablets mid-inspection?
  5. What is the exact PII field list for purge? (name, address, signature, photo EXIF?)
